saints.name: St. Oswald of Worcester
saints.title: Bishop
saints.shortBlurb: A reforming English bishop of Danish blood who renewed the monastic life of his land and died washing the feet of the poor…
biography: Born about 925 of Danish stock and brought up by his uncle St. Oda, archbishop of Canterbury, Oswald was sent about 950 to the abbey of Fleury in France to learn the monastic life, and was ordained there in 959. Recalled to England, he found his uncle dead, but St. Dunstan procured his consecration as bishop of Worcester in 961.

With Dunstan and St. Ethelwold of Winchester he was a chief worker in the monastic revival under King Edgar. He replaced the married clerks of Worcester cathedral with monks, and founded the abbey of Ramsey about 971 on land given by the ealdorman Aethelwine, bringing Abbo of Fleury to teach in its school.

In 972 he was made archbishop of York while retaining Worcester, holding both until his death. His Lenten custom was to wash and feed the poor each day; on 29 February 992, kneeling at that service in Worcester, he died, and was buried in the church of St. Mary; because his day recurs only in leap years, his feast is commonly kept on 28 February.
saints.knownFor: The English Benedictine revival with Saints Dunstan and Ethelwold.

sources.text: Butler, Lives of the Saints (1866 ed.), 28 February
